Team —

I need HR + recruiting help reconciling the feedback for Sofia Ramirez (applied for SWE role). Two interviewers came back with very different reads: Priya rated her as a strong match for the role we scoped (L3 / IC2), Mark called out several gaps and recommended not moving forward. The problem: the hiring doc shows an informal "consensus" for a higher band (L4) that I didn't sign off on.

I've attached the resume and the raw notes we have so far (interview-notes-priya.pdf, interview-notes-mark.pdf). My concerns:
- The divergence seems driven by scope of the system-design prompt Priya used vs the narrower alg/perf question Mark used.
- The recommended band on the packet appears to be the recruiter default (L4) but neither of my peers who will ultimately partner with this hire recommended L4.

Requesting:
1) Hold any offer extension until we reconcile the feedback.
2) HR to advise on leveling / appeals path and whether a calibration panel is required.
3) If useful, schedule a second technical screen for a consistent design prompt.

I want to avoid blind-banding a candidate without a clear calibration step — happy to join a short sync later today if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Engineering Manager, Edge Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks for escalating, Alex.

Two quick policy points so we have clarity on options:
1) Leveling appeals: hiring managers can request a calibration within 5 business days of final round debrief. HR convenes a cross-functional panel if debrief notes remain irreconcilable. See attached leveling-appeals-process.pdf for the formal steps.
2) Offer holds: Recruiting may place an offer "on hold" while calibration or an additional technical assessment is scheduled; we try to keep hold windows under 7 business days unless there's a clear exception.

Action items I propose now:
- Monica, please share anonymized excerpts from both interviewers' notes in the calibration meeting (no candidate PII beyond resume).
- Alex + Lauren: please confirm two times you can do a 30-min calibration today or tomorrow; if calibration doesn't resolve, confirm whether you prefer (A) a targeted system-design screen or (B) an invite to an engineering bar-raiser for a broader take.

If we go with a second screen, HR will provide a rubric aligned to L3 vs L4 criteria so the interviewer knows the decision axis.

I'll block time for a calibration slot and mark the role's offer status as "on hold" until we have a resolution; please treat this as high priority because the candidate is active with other processes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
People Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: leveling-appeals-process.pdf

Neha / Monica —

Thanks. I reviewed Priya and Mark's notes this morning and pulled a short reconciliation doc (copied into the calendar invite). Topline: Priya's prompt emphasized cross-service design and trade-offs; Mark's prompt focused on a tight algorithmic optimization where Sofia performed less well. Both are valid data points, but they map to different capability axes.

I recommend we perform a focused second technical screen that covers system design (L3 expectations: end-to-end tradeoffs, latency/cost, scaling strategy). If Sofia demonstrates consistent L3-level answers in that second loop, I'm comfortable authorizing L3 band and moving to offer. If not, we will close the loop without extending an offer.

Please proceed to schedule the second screen and send the candidate a short note about the slight scheduling delay. Happy to join the calibration as well.

Alex
